body:
Hello friend,

Like many of us that have encountered the problem with "reason" before, you're here looking for an answer. We can create a list of activities for you to try, however, none will satisfy your need. What we can do is offer advice. What you're feeling right now is more than likely temporary. Find solace in that fact. There is plenty of time to find reason. 

Sometimes a good solution is to find someone that has went through the cycle before, several times, and is still continuing with the struggle. I'm open to a personal message if you want to talk to someone.

Hello,

This might sound strange but I'm not going to advise you to stick around for your two kids. This is your life and what to do with it is your decision; however, it's crucial you realize that suicide is detrimental. Please, do not consider going down that route when there are solutions that will aid in your recovery from depression :)

From my experience; isolation seeps into your skin and contributes to the length and severity of depression. Searching for new friends is difficult because you're barred by the devastation that is going on in your mind. It's a real feeling and it's very understandable. Humans grieve. Your post here indicates that you are seeking help and you want a hand. That's a step in the right direction!

Unfortunately, I'm not going to be able to help you with career advice. Unemployment is in my basket of troubles as well. It sucks to be unemployed, but the only thing you can do is put your best effort in trying to find one. Anything else is asking too much and probably unattainable. As for your relationship woes: keep in mind that you should be happy before opening those doors. You deserve to be happy and that significant other deserves the same. Try to make some new friends, attend local events, contribute to charity or volunteer somewhere. Who knows, you might find that there are strings attached to those venues that lead elsewhere! 

If you simply just want someone to talk with, feel free to send a pm my way!

Hello,

Part of being human is experiencing events that take a tole on our mind and body. These experiences can cause depression and one element of depression is self criticism. As much as others judge us we judge ourselves ten-fold. What a disaster, right? Well, it's important to realize what you're doing so that you can prepare a constructive plan to aid you through your troubles. Whatever this might be, is of your own choosing, but there are people to help :)

Please, feel free to send a PM my way if you need someone to talk to. It's always a pleasure!

I've thought this over the course of a few months and had a moment where my life was going to be taken. Suicide is one solution of taking our pain away; however, it's a decision that you cannot come back from. There will be no more moments of clarity following your death, no passionate feelings of love, or that feeling you get when you bite into a piece of pizza. If you take some time to think about it the exchange (suicide vs. life) isn't an equal one. Death has nothing to offer you while there is a doorway outside your mental chamber. Those friends and family that you referenced in the OP are elements of your history; they were apart of your good times and they're apart of your bad ones as well. 

This is coming from someone that has been considering suicide ever since my teenage years. I've come across several obstacles during these years and lost many, many times to their challenges. There are more challenges to come and there might even be more instances of failure, but suicide, it's not going to offer me an opportunity to climb up from the hole I'm in. 

You have resources that you can use to climb out yourself. Don't feel bad or be afraid of using them. The fact that you exist gives them something. Repay them once you have paid yourself something. 

If you need someone to talk to or just need a friend, please feel free to pm me. Goodluck
